summary: This work demonstrates a parametric iSWAP gate between transmon qubits coupled via a double transmon coupler (DTC), achieving 99.827% fidelity in 40 ns operation. The DTC provides an internally-defined cancellation point that robustly suppresses static coupling and cross-Kerr interactions without requiring fine-tuning of capacitive coupling.
motivation: High-fidelity parametric gates are challenging because exchange interactions do not commute with single-qubit errors, demanding stringent phase stability and cross-Kerr compensation; iSWAP gates are particularly desirable for reducing circuit depth and enabling fault-tolerant surface codes with fewer couplers.
method: The DTC suppresses the effective coupling $g_\mathrm{eff}(\Phi_c)$ via competing capacitive $g_C$ and flux-tunable inductive $g_L(\Phi_c)$ interactions between two coupler transmons, operating the data qubits at the flux bias where $g_\mathrm{eff}=0$ minimizes residual cross-Kerr to $g_\mathrm{zz}=-2\pi\times220$ kHz. A novel robust phase estimation (RPE) routine calibrates non-commuting error terms (pump amplitude $\theta_p$, Stark shifts $\theta_1,\theta_2$, and cross-Kerr $\phi_\mathrm{zz}$) by designing compound gates that selectively amplify specific errors while suppressing unwanted state rotations, avoiding numerical optimization.
result: Process tomography yields gate fidelity of 99.827(±0.004)% at 40 ns; interleaved two-qubit randomized benchmarking confirms 99.70% fidelity. The measured fidelity is limited by data qubit decoherence ($T_1^{(1)}=26.35$ µs, $T_1^{(2)}=17.0$ µs, $T_2^{(1)}=15.02$ µs, $T_2^{(2)}=17.11$ µs) with a decoherence-limited upper bound of 99.72%, while residual $g_\mathrm{zz}$ contributes only 0.002% error.
